subject: Payroll query - new employee tax code and possible over-deduction for EMP-0091
body:
Hi,

We have two payroll matters that require your assistance:

1. New starter - James Whitfield joins on June 16, 2026. His previous employer has not yet issued a P45. Should we apply the emergency tax code 1257L W1/M1 in the meantime, or would you recommend a different approach to avoid under or over-taxation?

2. Existing employee over-deduction - Employee ref EMP-0091 (Maria Santos) believes she has been over-deducted on National Insurance contributions for the past three months. Her gross salary is £3,800 per month. Could you review her payroll records and advise on whether a correction is needed and how to process the refund?

We run payroll on the 25th of each month, so we would appreciate a response before June 24th.

Thanks,
HR Team
Metroplex Inc

subject: VAT return Q1 2026 - need your assistance preparing the submission
body:
Hello,

We need your assistance preparing our VAT return for Q1 2026 (January to March). Our figures for the quarter are as follows:

- Total turnover: £428,000
- Standard-rated sales: £386,000
- Zero-rated exports to EU clients: £42,000
- Input VAT on purchases: £18,200
- Output VAT on standard-rated sales: £77,200

We are unsure how to classify the zero-rated EU exports correctly on the return following the changes introduced after Brexit. We are also seeking clarification on whether our new online marketplace commissions qualify for input VAT recovery.

The VAT period ends June 30 and the filing deadline is July 7. Could you prepare the draft return and advise before we submit?

Best,
Finance Team
Nordica Retail Ltd

subject: Formal complaint - errors in 2024 accounts and unjustified fees
body:
I am writing to formally raise a complaint about the standard of service received from your firm.

Following an internal review of our 2024 annual accounts, we identified the following errors which your team was responsible for preparing:

1. Capital allowances of £12,400 were omitted entirely from the computation, resulting in an overpayment of corporation tax.
2. Three expense categories were incorrectly classified, affecting both the profit figure and tax liability.
3. We were invoiced for work that was outside the agreed scope of engagement and was never authorised.

We are requesting a full review of the 2024 accounts, correction of all errors, a tax refund for the overpayment, and reimbursement of the fees charged for the unauthorised work.

I expect a formal written response within 5 business days. If I do not receive a satisfactory resolution, I will have no choice but to escalate this matter to the Institute of Chartered Accountants.

Peter Walsh
Client Co Ltd

subject: R&D tax credit refund of £23,450 - still outstanding after 4 months
body:
Hi,

We submitted our R&D tax credit claim for the 2024-25 tax year back in February 2026. It has now been four months and we still have not received the refund of £23,450 from HMRC.

We were advised at submission that processing typically takes 6-8 weeks. We are now well beyond that timeframe and the delay is causing significant cash flow problems for the business. We have a payroll run on June 25th that we are struggling to cover.

Could you please follow up with HMRC on our behalf as a matter of urgency and provide an estimated timeline for payment? If there is an issue with the claim, we need to know immediately so it can be resolved.

Thank you,
Claire Dobson
Startup XYZ Ltd

subject: General questions about self-assessment tax return - first time filing
body:
Hello,

I recently started as a sole trader offering IT consulting services, and this will be my first time completing a self-assessment tax return. I am finding the process quite confusing and would appreciate some guidance.

Specifically, I have questions about:
1. What records I need to keep throughout the tax year (receipts, invoices, mileage logs, etc.)
2. Which expenses I can legitimately claim when I work primarily from home
3. Whether I can claim for equipment I purchased before I registered as self-employed
4. Key deadlines I should be aware of for 2025-26

I am not sure if I need an accountant at this stage or whether I can manage this myself. Would you be able to advise?

Many thanks,
Tom Bradley

subject: New client enquiry - would like to engage your accounting services
body:
Dear team,

I was recommended to your firm by a mutual contact, David Briggs at Briggs & Partners. I am the owner of New Horizons Catering Ltd, a small hospitality business that I started in January 2026.

I currently do not have an accountant and I am looking to engage a professional firm to handle our bookkeeping, payroll, annual accounts, and corporation tax return going forward.

We have 6 employees and turnover for this year is projected at approximately £280,000. I would also like advice on whether we should register for VAT at this stage.

Could you please send me information about your services and pricing, and advise on the next steps to get started? I am available for an initial consultation at any time.

Kind regards,
Emily Hayes
Director, New Horizons Catering Ltd

subject: Concerned about late filing penalty - what are our options?
body:
Hi,

I am writing with some urgency as I have just realised that our company's corporation tax return for the year ending 31 March 2025 may have been filed late. We submitted it on 6 January 2026, but I have just read that the deadline was 31 December 2025.

If this is the case, we understand a £100 penalty has already been levied. We are worried about further penalties if HMRC escalates this. Could you please:

1. Confirm whether the filing was indeed late
2. Advise on the penalty position and whether any mitigation is available
3. Confirm there are no other outstanding obligations we may have missed

This is causing me significant concern and I would appreciate an urgent response.

David Park
Park & Co Consulting

subject: Question about capital gains tax on property sale - follow-up
body:
Hello,

Following up on my earlier enquiry about capital gains tax on the sale of my investment property. I am now ready to proceed and would like proper advice before I file.

To recap: I sold my investment property in March 2026. Purchase price in 2018 was £320,000. Sale price £490,000. I spent £25,000 on qualifying improvements over the years.

I have since discovered I may also qualify for Private Residence Relief for the period I lived there (2018-2020), and I would like to understand how this affects my CGT computation.

Could you please review my situation and advise on:
1. The net taxable gain after all available reliefs
2. Whether I should use the 28% or 24% CGT rate
3. The filing and payment deadline for the CGT report

I understand the payment deadline may be approaching soon, so I would appreciate a response by next Friday.

Many thanks,
Mike Johnson

subject: Query about your service agreement, fees, and scope of engagement
body:
Dear team,

We are a medium-sized group of companies (3 entities) currently reviewing our professional services providers and considering switching accounting firms.

Before we proceed further, we would like to understand:

1. Your fee structure for managing annual accounts and corporation tax for a group of 3 companies with combined turnover of approximately £4.2m
2. Whether your engagement letter covers all entities in a group under a single agreement or separately
3. Your process for handling inter-company transactions and consolidation
4. Typical turnaround times for annual accounts preparation
5. Whether you offer a dedicated account manager

We would also appreciate a copy of your standard engagement terms and any client references from similar-sized businesses.

Best regards,
Procurement Team
Telford Group PLC

subject: Clarification needed on item in document checklist - depreciation schedule
body:
Hi,

Thank you for sending us the document checklist for our annual accounts preparation. I have gathered most of the items but I have a question about one of them.

The checklist asks for a 'depreciation schedule for all fixed assets.' We use a simple spreadsheet to track our assets but I am not sure if this is what you need, or whether you require something in a specific format.

We have:
- 12 company laptops (purchased 2023-2025)
- Office furniture (purchased 2022)
- Company van (purchased 2024, registered to the company)
- Some IT equipment that was fully written off in 2023

Could you clarify what information you need and in what format? I want to make sure I provide the right documents first time so we do not cause any delays.

Thank you,
Mark Sterling
Castleford Holdings Ltd
